contribution.value: PowerInfer is a GPU-CPU hybrid LLM inference engine that exploits power-law neuron activation, preloading hot neurons to GPU and computing cold neurons on CPU, reaching up to 11.69x speedup over llama.cpp on a single RTX 4090.

ev.quote: PowerInfer exploits such an insight to design a GPU-CPU hybrid inference engine: hot-activated neurons are preloaded onto the GPU for fast access, while cold-activated neurons are computed on the CPU

ev.quote: This paper introduces PowerInfer, a high-speed Large Language Model (LLM) inference engine on a personal computer (PC) equipped with a single consumer-grade GPU.
The key principle underlying the design of PowerInfer is exploiting the high locality inherent in LLM inference, characterized by a power-law distribution in neuron activation.
all models in our experiments use FP16 and INT4 quantized parameters, with intermediate activations in FP32

PowerInfer utilized general corpora such as Wikipedia [13] to train online activation predictors, Notably we deliberately avoided using any of the downstream task datasets in our predictor training process.

strengths.value: Up to 11.69x faster than llama.cpp on consumer RTX 4090 while keeping accuracy across multiple LLM families.

ev.quote: PowerInfer significantly outperforms llama.cpp by up to 11.69x while retaining model accuracy across various LLMs (including OPT-175B) on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU.

strengths.value: Reaches 82% of A100 token generation speed for OPT-30B on a $2,000 RTX 4090 vs $20,000 A100.

ev.quote: the inference speed achieved on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU (priced at approximately $2,000) is only 18% slower compared to the performance on a top-tier A100 GPU (costing around $20,000)

strengths.value: Adaptive predictors keep predictor parameters at only ~6-7% of LLM size, freeing GPU memory.

ev.quote: Through this approach, PowerInfer effectively limits predictor parameters to a mere 6% of the total LLM parameters.

strengths.value: Open-sourced and supports OPT, LLaMA2, Falcon families plus INT4 quantization on RTX 4090 and 2080Ti.

ev.quote: PowerInfer is compatible with various popular LLM families, including OPT (7B-175B), LLaMA2 (7B-70B), and Falcon-40B, and supports consumer-grade GPUs like the NVIDIA RTX 4090 and NVIDIA RTX 2080Ti.

weaknesses.value: Speedup drops sharply on SwiGLU/SiLU models (only 1.47x-1.7x) due to lower activation sparsity.

ev.quote: PowerInfer achieves a speedup of 1.47 x to 1.7x. This performance gain, albeit less pronounced than for ReLU-based counterparts

weaknesses.value: Long-prompt short-output cases give limited gains (1.07x-4x) as prompt phase dilutes activation sparsity.

ev.quote: In scenarios involving long input prompts with extremely short output lengths (less than 8 tokens), which are less common [35], PowerInfer demonstrates limited performance gains, ranging from 1.07x (Figure 11) to 4x

weaknesses.value: Speedup decreases as batch size grows beyond 32 because joint activations become denser.

ev.quote: As the batch size increases, the speed-up ratio offered by PowerInfer decreases. This reduction is attributed to the diminished sparsity of model joint activations.

weaknesses.value: On PC-Low (11GB GPU) gains are smaller than PC-High due to memory limits forcing more CPU work.

ev.quote: these improvements are smaller compared to those on a higher-end PC (PC-High), primarily due to the 11GB GPU memory limitation of PC-Low.

limitations.value: Targets local single-GPU PC inference with batch size near one; not designed for data-center high-throughput serving.

ev.quote: In contrast to data-center deployments, which prioritize high throughput [23, 43, 57], local deployments focus on low latency in processing small batches.

limitations.value: Effectiveness depends heavily on activation sparsity; non-ReLU models with under 50% sparsity see modest gains.

ev.quote: The effectiveness of PowerInfer is directly correlated with the model's activation sparsity. ReLU-family LLMs, exhibiting over 90% sparse activations in their FFNs, are ideal candidates for PowerInfer.

limitations.value: Predictor training is one-time but slow, often taking several hours and benefiting from multiple GPUs.

ev.quote: Training predictors, though time-consuming (often several hours), is a one-time task that can be expedited with multiple GPUs.

limitations.value: No reporting of energy consumption, edge-device tests, safety metrics, or long-context evaluation.

ev.quote: PowerInfer achieves up to 11.69x faster LLM inference compared to systems like llama.cpp, without compromising accuracy.

future_work_stated.value: Integrate speculative inference with PowerInfer to further boost LLM inference speed.

ev.quote: While separate from our focus, integrating speculative inference into PowerInfer could further boost LLM inference speed.

future_work_stated.value: Extend applicability through emerging ReLU-family activations (Nemotron, Mini-Tron) and sparsity-enhancing methods.

ev.quote: there is a growing trend on enhancing LLM sparsity without compromising performance [44, 46], or directly training LLMs with ReLU-family activations... This trend is expected to extend PowerInfer's applicability across a more diverse spectrum of LLMs.
